_note: 제목(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab/blank 의 밑줄·빈칸 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재. order/insert/irrelevant 는 구조 재배열.

passage: Until the 1950s, the tourism industry was deeply divided, with hotels, airlines, railways, and travel agencies all operating as fully separate businesses.
Hotels focused exclusively on providing overnight accommodation, while airlines and railways concentrated solely on selling seats.
Travel agents sold holidays and trips, yet each sector remained isolated, with no significant cooperation between them.
From the mid-1950s onward, especially in the United Kingdom, the emergence of tour operators began reshaping this landscape.
The industry's character shifted away from isolated operations toward a more connected and cooperative model.
Hotels, recognizing that guests wanted more than a bed, started adding shopping facilities and business support services.
Airlines also expanded their offerings, recognizing that transport was only one element of a broader travel experience.
By providing insurance and accommodation booking, airlines helped transform the industry into an integrated whole.
choices: the history of luxury hotel chains and their global expansion
how the tourism industry shifted from fragmented to integrated operations
challenges facing low-cost airlines in the modern travel market
the role of travel agents in managing customers' holiday expectations
why railways declined as air travel became more affordable
theme.explanation_ko: 글은 관광 산업이 1950년대 이전 분절된 구조에서 투어 오퍼레이터 성장을 계기로 통합된 구조로 변화했다는 내용. '분절에서 통합으로의 전환'인 ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①고급 호텔 체인 역사, ③저가 항공사 도전 과제, ④여행사의 고객 관리, ⑤철도의 쇠퇴는 본문의 초점이 아니다.

passage: Before the 1950s, the tourism industry was essentially a collection of unconnected businesses.
Hotels sold beds, airlines sold seats, and travel agents sold itineraries — each in isolation.
There was little sense that these businesses belonged to a single, unified industry.
The rise of tour operators from the mid-1950s, however, began to connect these separate pieces.
Hotels began offering a wider range of services; airlines began bundling transport with insurance and hotel reservations.
What had once been a fragmented set of transactions was becoming a seamless, integrated experience.
The tourism industry, in other words, discovered that its parts were stronger together.
Separation gave way to combination, and the tourism business was transformed.
choices: Hotels vs. Airlines: The Battle for the Modern Traveller
Separate to Combined: Changes in the Tourism Business
How Travel Agents Kept Tourism Alive in the Twentieth Century
The Decline of Railways and the Rise of Air Travel
Why Tour Operators Prefer Working Alone
title.explanation_ko: 글은 분절된(separate) 관광 산업이 통합된(combined) 형태로 변화했다는 내용으로, '분절에서 통합으로'를 직접 표현한 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①호텔 대 항공사의 경쟁, ③여행사의 역할, ④철도 쇠퇴, ⑤투어 오퍼레이터의 독립 선호는 본문 핵심과 다르다.

passage: Before the 1950s, tourism was very much an industry which was fragmented; hotels, transport operators, travel agents, and tour operators all tended to work independently of each other.
Hotels were largely in the business of selling bed nights.
Airlines and railways were in the business of selling seats.
Travel agents, of course, were selling travel and holidays, but in each case they tended to operate very much as individual businesses.

From the mid-1950s onwards, particularly in the UK, the growth of tour operators began to change the nature of the industry from essentially individual business activities to more integrated activities.
Hotels, for example, were beginning to see customers as wanting a range of services rather than simply buy accommodation.
So hotels began to develop shopping arcades and later to offer secretarial centres to try to increase the spend of guests within the hotel complex.
Transport operators, particularly in the airline business, saw the sale of transport services as being integral to a much wider need.
grammar.explanation_ko: ④ rather than 뒤에는 병렬 구조로 동명사(buying)가 와야 한다. 앞에 'wanting a range of services'(동명사)와 병렬이므로 'buy'를 'buying'으로 고쳐야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①계속적 관계절 which was fragmented, ②tend to + 동사원형 operate, ③begin to + 동사원형 change, ⑤see A as being B 구문 모두 어법상 옳다.

vocab.explanation_ko: ④ 호텔이 쇼핑 아케이드와 비서 센터를 도입한 목적은 투숙객의 지출을 '늘리기(increase)' 위함이다. decrease(줄이다)는 의도와 정반대 → increase로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①fragmented(분절된), ②independently(독립적으로), ③integrated(통합된), ⑤integral(불가결한)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: Before the 1950s, tourism was very much an industry which was fragmented; all sectors tended to work independently of each other.
Hotels sold bed nights, airlines and railways sold seats, and travel agents sold holidays — each as isolated businesses.
From the mid-1950s onwards, the growth of tour operators began to change this situation.
The industry shifted from individual, separate operations toward a more integrated approach.
Hotels started offering shopping arcades and secretarial centres to expand their guests' experience.
Transport operators saw selling transport as integral to a much wider need.
Airlines offered insurance and accommodation booking, connecting their services to the broader travel experience.
Thus, the industry moved from being essentially fragmented to being essentially integrated.
blank.explanation_ko: 앞에서 각 업체가 독립적으로 운영되었다(fragmented)고 했고, 뒤에서 통합(integrated) 방향으로 변화했다고 이어진다. 따라서 '개별적이고 분리된 운영(individual, separate operations)'에서 통합된 방향으로 변화했다고 해야 문맥이 자연스럽다.
blank.distractor_ko: ②정부 규제 독점, ③수익성 있는 국제 파트너십, ④고급 패키지, ⑤기술 기반 예약 플랫폼은 본문에서 언급된 변화 이전 상태와 무관하다.

order.given: Before the 1950s, tourism was very much an industry which was fragmented; hotels, transport operators, travel agents, and tour operators all tended to work independently of each other.

blocks.A: Hotels, for example, were beginning to see customers as wanting a range of services rather than simply buying accommodation, so they developed shopping arcades and secretarial centres to increase guests' spend.
blocks.B: From the mid-1950s onwards, particularly in the UK, the growth of tour operators began to change the nature of the industry from essentially individual business activities to more integrated activities.
blocks.C: Transport operators, particularly in the airline business, saw the sale of transport services as being integral to a much wider need, and airlines offered insurance and accommodation booking for travellers.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글(분절 상태)에 이어 (B)에서 1950년대 중반 이후 통합으로의 전환을 총론으로 제시하고, (A)에서 호텔의 통합 사례를, (C)에서 항공사의 통합 사례를 구체적으로 설명한다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 Hotels, for example이 (B)에서 제시된 통합 흐름의 예시이므로 (B) 뒤에 와야 하고, (C)의 항공사 사례는 호텔 사례(A) 이후의 또 다른 예시이다.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 글 전체의 결론(분절 → 통합)을 압축한 문장이다. 항공사의 보험·숙박 예약 제공(⑤ 앞)이 마지막 구체적 사례이고, 그 뒤에 총결론 문장이 오는 것이 자연스럽다.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장은 모든 구체적 예시(호텔·항공사)가 제시된 후에 와야 하므로 ⑤ 뒤가 적절하다. ①②는 분절 사례 중간이라 결론을 내리기 이르다.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 관광 산업이 분절에서 통합으로 변화한 과정을 다루는데, ③ '비자 규정의 강화'는 여행자 흐름 통제에 관한 것으로 산업 구조의 통합 변화와 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 모두 관광 산업의 통합 변화를 서술하는 흐름과 자연스럽게 연결된다.

passage: Before the 1950s, the tourism industry consisted of hotels, airlines, railways, and travel agents all operating in isolation.
Hotels sold accommodation, airlines and railways sold seats, and travel agents sold trips, each as separate businesses.
From the mid-1950s, the growth of tour operators began transforming the industry.
Hotels recognized that customers wanted a full range of services, not just a place to sleep.
They developed shopping arcades and secretarial centres to broaden their offerings.
Airlines understood that selling transport was part of a much wider travel need.
They started offering insurance and accommodation bookings alongside their flights.
The industry thus shifted from being fundamentally fragmented to being fundamentally integrated.
summary.summary_template: The tourism industry transformed from a __(A)__ collection of separate businesses into a(n) __(B)__ structure, as each sector expanded its services to meet the broader needs of travellers.
summary.explanation_ko: 관광 산업이 (A)fragmented(분절된) 상태에서 (B)integrated(통합된) 구조로 변화했다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 unified/profitable/regulated 가 아니라 fragmented, (B)는 isolated/competitive/diversified 가 아니라 integrated 여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그래서 관광 산업은 본질적으로 분절된 상태에서 본질적으로 통합된 상태로 이동했다.
writing.answer: So the tourism industry moved from being essentially fragmented to being essentially integrated.
writing.explanation_ko: from being A to being B 구조(전치사 from/to + 동명사 being). essentially(본질적으로)가 양쪽 형용사 모두에 적용.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 운송 업체들은 교통 서비스의 판매가 훨씬 더 광범위한 필요와 불가분의 관계에 있다고 보았다.
writing.answer: Transport operators saw the sale of transport services as being integral to a much wider need.
writing.explanation_ko: see A as being B(A가 B임을 보다). integral to(~에 불가결한). much는 비교급 wider를 강조.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 1950년대 중반 이후, 투어 오퍼레이터의 성장은 산업의 성격을 본질적으로 개별 사업 활동에서 보다 통합된 활동으로 바꾸기 시작했다.
conditions: from A to B 구조를 사용할 것
essentially 와 integrated 를 포함할 것
writing.answer: From the mid-1950s onwards, the growth of tour operators began to change the nature of the industry from essentially individual business activities to more integrated activities.
writing.explanation_ko: begin to change(바꾸기 시작했다), from essentially individual ... to more integrated(from A to B 전환 구조), essentially(본질적으로)와 integrated(통합된) 포함.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Hotels, for example, were beginning to see customers as wanting a range of services rather than simply buying accommodation.
writing.answer: 예를 들어, 호텔들은 단순히 숙박을 구매하는 것보다 오히려 다양한 서비스를 원하는 고객들을 바라보기 시작했다.
writing.explanation_ko: see A as + 동명사(wanting)(A를 ~하는 것으로 보다), a range of(다양한 종류의), rather than(~보다는).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Before the 1950s, the tourism industry was essentially (A)___________, with each sector working in isolation; but from the mid-1950s, it gradually became more (B)___________ as hotels and airlines expanded their services.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 1950년대 이전의 상태 → fragmented(분절된). (B) 1950년대 중반 이후의 변화 방향 → integrated(통합된).

writing.question: 다음 글의 주제를 <조건>에 맞게 한 문장의 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 관광 산업이 분절된 상태에서 통합된 상태로 변화한 과정
conditions: from과 to를 사용하여 변화를 표현할 것
writing.answer: The tourism industry transformed from a fragmented collection of businesses to an integrated structure.
writing.explanation_ko: from a fragmented ... to an integrated ...(분절에서 통합으로)로 변화 방향을 압축. transform(변화하다) 사용.
